A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spectrum Tuning research and provide readable methods, results, figures, tables, and extensive appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across Gemma, Qwen, and Llama, including steerability, diversity, distributional alignment, ablations, and human evaluation.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds training and data ablations in Table 4 and temperature-sweep experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same shuffled task examples, output-token cross-entropy, description dropout, and initialization scheme. The newly evaluated first-output-only and last-output-only variants are ablation comparators, not changes to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: The Spectrum Suite train, test, and capability source lists match. Both retain the same 22 verifiable generation tasks, two human-evaluation prompt sets, seven distributional-alignment datasets, and capability benchmarks. The added controls and temperature sweeps operate within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds first-output-only training inspired by Instruct-SFT, last-output-only training inspired by MetaICL, and capability-data and size-matched Spectrum Suite controls. It removes v1's untrained PT and IT models evaluated with ST prompts. The main pretrained and instruction-tuned comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds sampling temperatures of 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1, 1.5, 2, 5, and 10, plus matched training-data controls using 3.9k sequences. Existing primary evaluation settings remain unchanged. The explicit ECE formula and exact-string deduplication statement document existing metrics rather than establish changed procedures.

E4.justification: Section 7 substantially expands attribution analyses through loss-position and matched-data ablations. Appendix E tests whether diversity and yield advantages survive temperature optimization across models and prompting conditions. Two untrained ST-prompt controls are removed. The batch-size analysis already existed in v1 Appendix C and is retained in v2 Appendix H.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same 95% confidence and significance conventions, including the SEM-based intervals for the original diversity figure, and unchanged human agreement statistics. V2 adds no new run-count, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: New Table 4 entries report three-shot yields of 33.0 and 35.4 for first-output-only and last-output-only training, versus 42.1 for the default. Matched capability/Spectrum data yield JS divergences of 0.111/0.086. New temperature results show Spectrum Tuning achieves the highest attainable yield in eight of nine settings. Two ST-prompt result rows disappear; the main tables and retained batch-size results match.

T1.justification: The formal task formulation, exchangeability assumption, objective, and algorithm remain unchanged. V2 supplies formulas for existing ECE, validity, uniqueness, and yield metrics, without introducing new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: three distributional desiderata, Spectrum Suite, findings about post-training degradation, and Spectrum Tuning's benefits. Added motivation and experiments support rather than redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C adds hypotheses about reward maximization causing mode collapse and Spectrum Tuning counteracting pretrained n-gram biases. Section 7 interprets the new loss-position and data controls. Existing limitations concerning model size, chat performance, and safety are relocated without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds dataset-sourcing principles, Section 5 specifies exact-string deduplication, and Table 2 clarifies ECE calculation from label-token probabilities. New ablation sizes and temperature settings are documented. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, templates, and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bhatia et al. (2025), Value Drifts, when discussing investigation across post-training checkpoints. Related work adds a brief entropy-maximization statement using the already cited Li et al. (2025) and slightly clarifies the MetaICL relationship. Overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Section 7 is rewritten and reorganized, a short FAQ and data-construction explanation are added, and limitations and general-capability discussion move to appendices. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Author-name, conference-header, and small wording corrections also appear.

P2.justification: Table 4 is substantially redesigned into grouped comparisons with ablation identifiers and training-size columns. Two nine-panel temperature figures are added. V1 Figures 1–2 become v2 Figures A1–A2, and v1 Table 5 becomes v2 Table A1, substantially changing the distribution of displays between the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens v1's fixed-temperature evidence with temperature sweeps and adds controls that better distinguish the effects of training data and loss placement. These focused gains improve empirical support and explanation. Removing the two untrained ST-prompt controls reduces one diagnostic comparison, but the net benefit is positive; the main method, findings, and applicability limits remain unchanged.
